tasks.title: build.md Phase 5: release the goal/lock pair on every terminal path, push/PR failure included
tasks.description:
Fixes F-018. Repair the terminal-release ordering in plugin/commands/build.md Phase 5 so no terminal exit can leave .g2g-goal / .g2g-goal.lock armed after a failed push or gh pr create.

```finding excerpt (F-018)
Title: Phase 5 deletes .g2g-goal only after a fallible push/PR step
Description: On the terminal partial-stop path (Phase 5), the orchestrator is told to Push the branch once and open a DRAFT PR ... [release] before finishing — push/gh come first, [release] second, with no handling for a push or gh pr create failure. If the push fails (e.g. no origin remote, auth/network failure), the procedure has no abort branch that still [releases] .g2g-goal. In Phase 5 the goal condition is unmet (tasks not all passed), so the only way the session can stop is [releasing the pair]; leaving .g2g-goal armed means the Stop hook keeps blocking the session, and the run cannot cleanly terminate. This contradicts CLAUDE.md's invariant never leave a terminal path that skips [the release]. Notably the Phase 4 conflict path (step 5) already [releases] .g2g-goal FIRST, then aborts the rebase and pushes — showing the [release]-first pattern is intended; Phase 5 uses the risky order.
Suggestion: In Phase 5, [release] .g2g-goal before the push/PR step (mirroring the Phase 4 conflict path), or make the push/PR step's failure route explicit: on push or gh failure, still [release] .g2g-goal, then report the terminal outcome honestly (branch left local, no PR). Ensure every terminal path [releases] the pair regardless of whether the push/PR succeeds.
```

The release is performed by g2g-lock.sh release-terminal <owner-token> (build.md's current mechanism) — do not reintroduce hand deletion of the lock/goal files. Keep the existing exit-5 and other-nonzero handling of that helper call intact.
acceptanceCriteria: In plugin/commands/build.md Phase 5, the g2g-lock.sh release-terminal call is reachable on every terminal exit of the phase — including the path where 'git push' or 'gh pr create' fails — either by ordering the release before the push/PR (mirroring the Phase 4 conflict path at step 5) or by an explicit failure route that still runs release-terminal on push/gh failure before the session ends.
Reading Phase 5 shows no ordering in which the phase can finish with .g2g-goal/.g2g-goal.lock still present after a failed push or failed gh pr create.
The existing release-terminal exit-code handling (exit 5 = pair no longer yours, delete nothing; any other nonzero = report verbatim and leave for a human) is preserved unchanged.
No BUILDER REPORT / VERIFIER REPORT marker line or field is changed; g2g-lock.sh is not modified.
tasks.notes: Phase 5 release-terminal reordered to run before push/PR (step 1), mirroring Phase 4 conflict path; exit-5/nonzero handling preserved. make check 66/66.

tasks.title: Reconcile template models.builder with the documented sonnet default
tasks.description:
Fixes F-028. Make the shipped template builder-model value agree with the documented/coded default across all four templates.

```finding excerpt (F-028)
Title: Templates set models.builder to inherit, overriding the documented sonnet default
Description: README Config and build.md Phase 3 step 6 define the builder model default as sonnet, with an explicit design rationale (tasks are pre-decomposed with explicit criteria, a Sonnet-shaped job). But all four templates (g2g-node/python/bash/greenfield.json) ship models.builder=inherit. Because build.md only falls through to the sonnet default when the field is absent, every repo onboarded via /g2g:init gets builder=inherit, so the documented default and its cost rationale never take effect. The coded default, the documented default, and the shipped config value disagree.
Suggestion: Reconcile the three: either set builder:sonnet in the templates to match the documented/coded default, or omit the key so build.md's fall-through applies — and update README/build.md if inherit is actually the intended shipped behavior.
```

Pick one reconciliation and apply it consistently so no documentation states a sonnet builder default while a template ships otherwise. Do not alter defaultBudgets, reviewFocus, or improve.enabled in any template (tests/templates.bats pins those).
acceptanceCriteria: After the change, the builder-model default is consistent across all three sources: the four plugin/templates/g2g-*.json files, README Config, and build.md Phase 3 step 6 — no source claims a sonnet builder default while a template ships 'inherit'.
All four templates (g2g-node.json, g2g-python.json, g2g-bash.json, g2g-greenfield.json) are updated identically for the models.builder field.
defaultBudgets values, the five reviewFocus categories, and improve.enabled:false remain unchanged in every template.
tests/templates.bats passes, and make check passes.

tasks.title: Route the improve tick's cycle model via models.improveCycle
tasks.description:
Fixes F-033. Give the headless improve cycle its own configurable model instead of silently inheriting the operator's default CLI model.

```finding excerpt (F-033)
Title: Improve tick inherits the operator default model for its entire cycle
Description: The improve spawn passes no --model flag, so the whole headless cycle — orchestrator, all review category subagents, spec generation, and any builder/verifier not explicitly routed — runs on the invoking machine's default CLI model. When that default is a premium model, the tick's dominant costs (the review fan-out above all) are paid at premium rates. models.builder routing only covers builder dispatches, not the cycle itself.
Suggestion: Add tick-level routing: improve.md reads .claude/g2g.json models.improveCycle (default sonnet) and passes it as --model on the spawned claude -p invocation; improve-nightly.md mirrors it. Keep adversarial judgment premium where desired via the existing models.verifier field. Document in the runbook's budget section that tick cost scales directly with this model choice.
```

Scope: edit plugin/commands/improve.md (Launch spawn) and plugin/routines/improve-nightly.md only for the routing; document the new config key in plugin/README.md Config and note the cost relationship in docs/G2G_PLUGIN_REF.md's Budget section. Do NOT modify plugin/templates/*.json — the sonnet default applies via fall-through when models.improveCycle is absent (this keeps T-003 off the files T-002 edits).
acceptanceCriteria: plugin/commands/improve.md's Launch spawn resolves a cycle model from .claude/g2g.json → models.improveCycle, defaulting to sonnet when the file or field is absent, and passes it as --model <value> on the spawned 'claude -p' invocation.
plugin/routines/improve-nightly.md applies the same models.improveCycle resolution and --model passing on its spawn.
plugin/README.md Config documents the models.improveCycle field (purpose and sonnet default).
docs/G2G_PLUGIN_REF.md's Budget section notes that improve-tick cost scales with the models.improveCycle choice.
No file under plugin/templates/ is modified by this task.
